items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: I want to say that later on we asked who the hell that was, and that was Elvis Presly's first appearance on anything major

ctx.x: and set up in our section in the back, that hadn't revolved yet, with the long cameras, while we were setting up, we heard this (UNINTELLIGIBLE) of songs, we thought then, of the band ahead of us, the artist ahead of us, which we were to follow as the bandstand revolved, and we were all looking at each other -- the side glances, and asked us what kind of music was that and what's going on and we were set up, and we would do our segment when the bandstand turned, and we'd do our bit.

I want to say that later on we asked who the hell that was, and that was Elvis Presly's first appearance on anything major -- the powers to be arranged with the Gleason office that he was to be presented on that show, and that's the first time he ever appeared on television to my knowledge. And that was the beginning of the great Elvis.

I must remark that back at the theatre, the Paramount Theatre, Charlie Shavers and I confined our culinary efforts to having a standard order with Sardi's, which was next door, and we had a waiter service, and about the biggest thing we cooked was music.
